test_title: SSC Selection Post 2025 (Matriculation Level) Official Paper (Held On: 29 Jul, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:

This is the (1) / most easiest question (2) / in the entire (3) / test paper(4).
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error is found in **part 2** of the sentence due to the use of a **double superlative**.
 
• The adjective "**easy**" is a two-syllable word ending in 'y'. Its superlative form is created by changing the 'y' to 'i' and adding "**-est**" (i.e., **easiest**).
 
• In English grammar, it is incorrect to use "**most**" alongside an adjective that already has the superlative suffix "-est." This creates redundancy.
 
• The phrase "**most easiest**" should be corrected to simply "**easiest**."

Therefore, the correct answer is **2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"This is the **easiest** question in the entire test paper."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **(1) "This is the"** – This part is correct; the definite article "the" is required before a superlative adjective.
 
• **(3) "in the entire"** – This phrase is grammatically correct and serves to emphasize the scope of the comparison.
 
• **(4) "test paper."** – This is the object of the preposition "in" and is used correctly.
 
• **Rule for Superlatives:** Use "-est" for one-syllable adjectives and two-syllable adjectives ending in 'y'. Use "most" for adjectives with three or more syllables (e.g., "most difficult"). Never use both together.
